items.title: Norman Simmons interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 27, 2007 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Mr. Five by Five. I even worked with him in New York.

ctx.x: Mr. Five by Five. I even worked with him in New York. So that was that situation in Chicago. We all had this foundational blues thing. And a lot of clubs we worked in those particular days were show clubs. In other words it might have been a combo of four pieces, a horn and a rhythm section, but other than that you’d have a dancer and a comedian, and you know what I mean? So no telling who else would be on there. And so there was a mixture going on there. And so therefore, so when it came to calling musicians it…
Was it easier for a jazz musician to exist, to do a good job, in a blues setting than it would be for a blues musician to go to a jazz setting?
